summary: Gone Rich Mountain site in Greenbrier County, WV; only the FFLOS register and county list describe it. A Randolph County Rich Mountain tower moved to Snowshoe is a different site.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association's county list marks it Tower Gone; no source describes what remains.

events.note: Registered January 26, 2017, nominated by Brian M. Powell.
Listed as Tower Gone on the county list. No year or method is given.

evidence.supports: Greenbrier County, West Virginia location and elevation of 3,817 feet (1,163 meters)
administered by the West Virginia Division of Forestry
evidence.quote: Administered by West Virginia Division of Forestry

evidence.supports: tower is gone, per county list
Rich Mountain Battlefield trail near Beverly; tower taken apart and moved to Snowshoe Resort
evidence.quote: Rich Mountain Battlefield Trail (Beverly, WV – Rich Mountain Battlefield Association): Easy 0.5-mile walking trail. Tower disassembled and moved to Snowshoe Resort.

evidence.supports: the former Rich Mountain tower now stands at the privately owned Snowshoe Mountain ski resort
evidence.quote: The former Rich Mountain Fire Tower now stands at the privately owned Snowshoe Mountain ski resort.

sources.title: Walking the Old Watch: Former Fire Tower Hikes in the Mon

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rich Mountain also names a Randolph County tower. Sources tie a Rich Mountain tower from the Battlefield trail near Beverly to Snowshoe, which is not this Greenbrier County site.

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLOS register page, the FFLOS county list, one Mon Forest article and the NHLR Snowshoe page were usable; two searches added nothing about this site. No build date, staffing, fire or access source found, so access is omitted. The brief's status 'gone' matches the county list. The Randolph County Rich Mountain (FFLOS US 1690, listed Tower Gone) is a separate record and was not researched here. No photos found.
